metadata.description: Materials Project entries removed from every fetched or cached convex hull. 'elements': elemental structures with no stability field at 1 atm at any temperature (high-pressure, thin-film or purely computational), keyed by element and matched by material_id or by (element, spacegroup_number). 'compounds': rules for non-elemental artifacts, each with one 'match' predicate: 'material_id', 'composition' (exact atom counts in the cell) or 'element_count' (counts of the named elements only). 'expected_gs_spacegroup': each element's 1-atm ground-state space group; an elemental entry below it with another space group is also removed.
metadata.policy: Each elemental entry has no reported ambient-pressure stability field (NIST TN 2312, D.R. Burgess Jr., 'Phase Transition Temperatures of the Solid Elements at Atmospheric Pressure', 2025). Real low-temperature allotropes are not listed.

Ag.reason: Thin-film and nanostructure polytype only; Ag is FCC from 0 K to melting at 1 atm.
Ag.source: NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=47; Fan et al., Nat. Commun. 6, 7684 (2015)

Ta.reason: Metastable sputtered thin-film phase; bulk Ta is BCC at all temperatures at 1 atm.
Ta.source: Jiang et al., Thin Solid Films 479, 166 (2005); Magnuson et al., Appl. Surf. Sci. 470, 607 (2019); Nnolim, Tyson & Axe, J. Appl. Phys. 93, 4543 (2003)

Ta.reason: The same thin-film beta-Ta phase under the alternative space group P-42_1m (favoured by Arakcheeva et al.); removed with mp-569794 so that neither becomes the ground state.
Ta.source: Arakcheeva, Chapuis & Grinevitch, Acta Crystallogr. B 58, 1 (2002); Magnuson et al., Appl. Surf. Sci. 470, 607 (2019)

Rb.reason: High-pressure phases only (16 GPa and above); Rb is BCC from 0 K to melting at 1 atm.
Rb.source: NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=37; McMahon, Rekhi & Nelmes, Phys. Rev. Lett. 87, 055501 (2001)

Sr.reason: The reported hcp interval is a hydrogen-contamination artifact; pure Sr is fcc, then bcc above 820 K.
Sr.source: Peterson & Colburn, J. Phys. Chem. 70, 468 (1966); NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=38; Alcock, Chase & Itkin, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 22, 1 (1993)

Eu.reason: High-pressure (12 GPa and above) or thin-film phase; Eu is BCC from 0 K to melting at 1 atm.
Eu.source: Bi et al., Phys. Rev. B 83, 104106 (2011)

Eu.reason: Matches no experimentally known Eu phase; a computational structure below the real BCC.
Eu.source: Bi et al., Phys. Rev. B 83, 104106 (2011)

Lu.reason: High-pressure phase (above ~23 GPa); Lu is HCP from 0 K to melting at 1 atm.
Lu.source: Liu, J. Phys. Chem. Solids 36, 31 (1975); NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=71

Pr.reason: High-pressure phase (above ~4 GPa); at 1 atm Pr is dhcp, then bcc above 1068 K.
Pr.source: NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=59; Konings & Beneš, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 39, 043102 (2010); Evans et al., Phys. Rev. B 80, 134105 (2009)

Pr.reason: Distorted-fcc high-pressure phase (~7-10 GPa); no ambient-pressure field.
Pr.source: Vohra, Vijayakumar, Godwal & Sikka, Phys. Rev. B 30, 6205 (1984); Evans et al., Phys. Rev. B 80, 134105 (2009)

Pr.reason: Disputed monoclinic phase reported only above ~10 GPa and ruled out by later XRD; no ambient-pressure field.
Pr.source: Chesnut & Vohra, Phys. Rev. B 62, 2965 (2000); Evans et al., Phys. Rev. B 80, 134105 (2009)

In.reason: Undistorted parent of the real body-centred-tetragonal In structure, which stays tetragonal up to melting.

C.reason: Stacking-fault variant of hexagonal graphite, metastable at all conditions; hexagonal graphite is the reference state.
C.source: Boehm & Coughlin, Carbon 2, 1 (1964); Lipson & Stokes, Proc. R. Soc. A 181, 101 (1942)

Hg.reason: Matches none of the known Hg polymorphs; a computational structure.
Hg.source: Young, Phase Diagrams of the Elements, University of California Press (1991)

Hg.reason: High-pressure gamma-Hg, stable only between 12 and 37 GPa.
Pressure-formed phase (above ~1.2 GPa) retained metastably at low temperature; TN 2312 lists alpha-Hg as the only solid at 1 atm (Atoji et al. 1959 report beta-Hg as stable below 79 K).
Hg.source: Atoji, Schirber & Swenson, J. Chem. Phys. 31, 1628 (1959); Schulte & Holzapfel, Phys. Rev. B 48, 14009 (1993); Young, Phase Diagrams of the Elements (1991)

Ti.reason: High-pressure phase (alpha to omega at several GPa) retained metastably after decompression; at 1 atm Ti is hcp below 1155 K and bcc to melting. GGA places it 15 meV/atom below hcp.
Ti.source: NIST TN 2312 (2025), Z=22; Sikka, Vohra & Chidambaram, Prog. Mater. Sci. 27, 245 (1982); Mei et al., Phys. Rev. B 80, 104116 (2009)

compounds.reason: A giant-cell composition artifact that displaces real Mg-X line compounds; matches any entry with exactly 149 Mg atoms.
compounds.source: gliquid legacy filter; no upstream Materials Project report on record
